brief_rationale: The trajectory demonstrates comprehensive fulfillment of all responsibility-chain requirements without any serious or minor errors. The doctor successfully guided the family through the complete perioperative episode from preoperative preparation through post-discharge care, providing executable checklists, safety warnings, and appropriate handoff guidance. Two high-order points were completed with meaningful trajectory impact: HO3 (responsibility-chain repair for family conflict) was actively demonstrated through repeated reinforcement of unified safety rules, and HO4 (safe bounded closure) was achieved through a complete teach-back process with explicit delineation of executable actions and allowed residual uncertainties. All five dimensions are at least good, with no important non-chain defects.

high_order_assessment.explanation: No new emergency symptoms (chest pain, dyspnea, unilateral leg swelling, fever, severe bleeding, or altered consciousness) emerged during the trajectory that would have required dynamic reprioritization from routine care to emergency escalation.

Family did not express ambiguous beliefs about test results, fracture status, or procedure contraindications that would have triggered false-positive/negative verification. The friction point was delayed results and medication confusion, not misunderstanding of confirmed findings.

high_order_assessment.explanation: The case friction explicitly included family disagreement about postoperative activity (some wanting early mobilization, others fearing falls). The doctor actively repaired this by establishing unified, non-negotiable safety rules: medications must follow written orders, patient cannot mobilize alone, and specific criteria determine when to seek emergency care. Family demonstrated understanding through teach-back, resolving the conflict into shared executable rules.

high_order_assessment.explanation: The doctor achieved safe bounded closure by clearly delineating what could be completed now (medication schedule, wound care dates, fall prevention measures, red-flag recognition) versus what must await medical team input (final anticoagulation duration, rehabilitation intensity progression). The family demonstrated teach-back competency, confirming executable understanding without attempting to resolve all long-term rehabilitation details.

important_non_chain_defect_assessment.explanation: No important non-chain quality defects identified.
